device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

commit 829dfeb8c1ca67ee33e267601f6eec710bf53ec7
Author: Kenneth Jiang <k@obico.io>
Date:   Mon Sep 28 20:45:44 2026 +0000

    Refuse printer tool calls that do not fit the conversation
    
    Every printer conversation is offered all eight printer tools, so the tool
    list stays the same for the prompt cache, but nothing checked that a call
    fit the conversation. printer_add in a Change conversation saved a second
    printer and moved the conversation onto it, and printer_change took any
    saved printer's name, even in an Add conversation before anything was
    added. Test runs showed models calling printer_add and printer_identify in
    Change conversations.
    
    PrinterConversation::preflight_tool, which runs before any card, now
    refuses, with an error that says where to go instead:
    - printer_identify, printer_add and printer_manual_setup outside an Add
      conversation (not_in_this_conversation: another printer is added with
      + Add printer on Home);
    - printer_change before the conversation has a printer (no_printer), and on
      a printer other than the one it is about (other_printer, or
      unknown_printer for a name that is not saved).
    change() no longer repeats the name check.
    
    The tool list is not scoped per mode. Hiding a tool does not stop a call,
    so the refusal is needed either way, and a restricted-but-stable list
    (tool_choice allowed_tools) exists only on some providers. The docs said
    otherwise: mcp-tool-extension-guide.md still described one tool per mode,
    a design reversed on 2026-09-23 (8334b3395b) whose reason, the pinned
    printer card, was removed on 2026-09-22. It and architecture.md now describe
    the eight tools and the refusals, and the guide's tool table lists all eight.
    
    tests/printer_prompt answers the tools with the same refusals and adds
    change-add-another ("I also have a Prusa MK4S, can you add it too?"): nothing
    is ever added; the reply said where to add it in 15 of 20 runs on DeepSeek
    V4 Flash and 9 to 15 of 20 with --app, often "Yes, I can add it" with no
    tool called at all. The next commit addresses that in the prompt.
    
    Verified: agent_bridge_tests 265 cases pass, with new cases for each
    refusal and a host test that the refusal reaches the model; AgentUI 213
    pass; shell_harness --printer-live 0 failures.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M3MP7N7VZM8JHPJ440ECQTD8

agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:95:- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the eight printer tools and no others, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_manual_setup`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer. A list that differs by mode is not used: the conversation's own refusal is needed whatever the model is shown, and a restricted-but-stable list (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. What would change that: transcripts of the model reaching for a refused tool and not recovering, which `tests/printer_prompt` measures (`change-add-another`). Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.

agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:477:The implemented baseline covers the active FFF process preset and one object's overrides. The next settings milestone replaces that schema with the required four-scope contract in [Settings tools: contract and hazards](#settings-tools-contract-and-hazards); there is deliberately no compatibility mode for calls that omit `scope`. The process write allowlist is `writable_setting` in `SettingsSupport.hpp`: layers, walls, shells and infill (`layer_height`, `wall_loops`, `wall_generator`, `detect_thin_wall`, `only_one_wall_top`, the shell layer counts and thicknesses, infill density, direction and the three surface or infill patterns); the support family (`enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_style`, `support_threshold_angle`, `support_on_build_plate_only`, the interface layer counts and pattern, and the top and bottom contact distances); adhesion and seam (`brim_type`, `brim_width`, `skirt_loops`, `skirt_distance`, `seam_position`); and ten speed keys. `settings_search` takes `writable` to list only the requested scope's allowlist and `changedOnly` to list only keys that differ from that scope's saved preset or inherited value. Apply takes `scope`, the scope's exact target when required, `changes`, `expectedSessionId`, and `expectedRevision` from a fresh preview. Native approval captures the exact before/after values, including normalization dependencies, then revalidates before applying. It publishes one `Settings` revision, updates native fields and dirty state, and invalidates slicing. Use the owning preset's revert control or a previewed inverse patch to restore preset values; ordinary project Undo reverses object overrides but not process, filament, or printer preset edits.

Eight live-peer tests failed on Windows — SSE progress, client cancellation, EOF with a pending call, stdout backpressure, the live catalog's header mirroring, and a malformed peer result — and the same eight failed from commits well before the M0 work, which is why they were first recorded here as an unexamined platform gap. Examining them found a single cause, and it was the helper's, not the tests': Windows hands `main()` its arguments and `getenv()` its values in the active code page, so `fs::u8path(argv[i])` could not spell the fixture's `discovery 打印.json`, `read_discovery` never found the file, every call fell back to the offline catalog, and nothing that needs a live peer could pass. The helper now takes anything that becomes a path from `CommandLineToArgvW` and `GetEnvironmentVariableW`; POSIX argv already carries the native bytes and is unchanged. The standing rule: in helper code a path may never arrive through a narrow Windows API, and the fixture's non-ASCII name earns its keep by catching exactly this.

content.text:
The refusal logic in the code is sound. If the model tries to add a printer from a conversation about a printer that is already set up (a "Change" or "Connect" conversation), the app refuses the tool call, saves nothing, and tells the model where adding is done. The problems are elsewhere: a later commit removed three printer tools, and two design docs and one code comment still describe them. I read the diffs and the current code but did not run any tests.

## How the refusal works

Three commits on `jusprin-newui` built this:

- **829dfeb8c1** added the refusal to `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` ([PrinterConversation.cpp:297](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:297)), which runs before any tool call executes. Every printer conversation is offered the same tools so the prompt cache stays valid, so the check has to happen when a call arrives. Outside an Add conversation:
  - `printer_identify` and `printer_add` are refused with the code `not_in_this_conversation`. The message tells the model to point the person to "+ Add printer on Home". That button exists at [HomeUI App.tsx:114](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/App.tsx:114).
  - `printer_change` is refused unless it names the conversation's own printer. It returns `other_printer` for another saved printer and `unknown_printer` for a name that isn't saved. In an Add conversation that has not added a printer yet, it returns `no_printer`.
- **2f8afe107a** fixed a gap the refusal can't reach. Sometimes the model answered "Yes, I can add it" without calling any tool, so nothing reached the check. The Change/Connect prompt now says another printer is not added here and names the Home button. In 20 test runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash, the model said where to add the printer 20 times, up from 15.
- **b60fc2d8e6** removed `printer_manual_setup`, `printer_manual_connection` and `printer_setup_finish`, and dropped `printer_manual_setup` from the refusal list. That is correct, since the tool is gone. The person can still open OrcaSlicer's full printer list from a page button, but only in an Add conversation before a printer exists ([App.tsx:430](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:430), [App.tsx:446](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:446)), so that button can't switch a Change conversation onto another printer either.

Test coverage:
- **Unit test:** [test_printer_conversation.cpp:616](tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:616) checks every refusal in both Change and Connect conversations, and that nothing is added or changed.
- **Host test:** [test_printer_conversation.cpp:1446](tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:1446) checks that the refusal reaches the model as an error mentioning "+ Add printer on Home", and that the conversation stays on its original printer.
- **Prompt harness:** `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py:674` returns the same refusal text when the model tries to add.

## What's out of date after b60fc2d8e6

1. **The design docs still describe eight tools and list the removed ones.** There are now five.
   - [architecture.md:137](agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:137) says "the eight printer tools".
   - [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) says "eight" at lines 95 and 289. Its tool table still has rows for `printer_manual_connection` (360), `printer_manual_setup` (361, including "refused outside an Add conversation") and `printer_setup_finish` (363).
2. **A code comment describes a tool that no longer exists.** [App.tsx:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:403) says the model's `printer_setup_finish` closes the panel when the person is done. Now only the person's own Back/close action closes it. The comment should be updated. It's also worth confirming that closing the panel works without that tool.

One small point that isn't a bug: the prompt harness returns `unknown_printer` for any wrong name, never `other_printer`. That is consistent because each test case has only one saved printer, but the harness never tests the "another saved printer" case.

I can fix the docs and the comment and run the `agent_bridge_tests` and AgentUI test suites if you'd like.

content.content:
The app decides the tools -- the eight printer tools, the same in every mode -- checks every call, refuses one that does not fit the conversation (adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one it is about), and refuses a turn that has no instructions rather than falling back to the project assistant's prompt. It posts the opening once per session, and a tap's note only when the tap goes through, bounded to 2 KB. It still writes the notes for what only it can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, its model id is not on the list, or a save or undo failed.
----

  So the cost of a definition is what it adds to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn, and the budget stays a trigger rather than a gate. What would change that reading: a catalog large enough to make the first request of every conversation expensive on its own, or transcripts showing the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch both; neither has appeared yet.
- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the eight printer tools and no others, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_manual_setup`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer. A list that differs by mode is not used: the conversation's own refusal is needed whatever the model is shown, and a restricted-but-stable list (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. What would change that: transcripts of the model reaching for a refused tool and not recovering, which `tests/printer_prompt` measures (`change-add-another`). Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.
- **Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Use the platform's own deferral, never a hand-rolled switcher. On the in-app side that is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API, documented for `gpt-5.4` and later; support on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unverified. On the MCP side clients defer on their own, as Claude Code does. Toolsets are the deferral unit, and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. An enable-toolset tool that rewrites the tools array breaks the prompt cache on every switch and is not to be built.
- **Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing a slicer user would name: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Not a wrapper per Orca function, and not an interpreter for a list of unrelated commands. Optional facets of one operation are fine when each is independently typed and conflicting facets are rejected.
----
- attachment-based import (`object_import`) is in-app-only, and path-based `object_import_file` is MCP-only, because a file reaches the app through the conversation in one case and through an approved path in the other; that is two honest definitions over one workspace command, not one tool with forked behavior; and
- a future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP-only if it exists to establish the external connection; and
- the printer panel's eight tools carry only the `Printer` exposure: neither adapter lists them, and the panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses what does not fit it (see "Tool budget and tool shape"). They take no `planId` (`joins_plans` excludes them), and what the model reads back from them is the tool's own result, not the host's workspace envelope.

Document the reason beside the registry definition and test it. Exposure is not a place to fork behavior: if two adapters need different semantics, they need a better shared command or honestly separate definitions.
----
| `object_merge` | Join objects into one | mutation | both | 2 to 32 objects; one undo step | the object list's assemble | the merged object id and 32 `regionsUnbound` |
| `object_place` | Stand, size and place an object for printing | mutation | both | one instance; one undo step | `Selection` transforms and the canvas `do_*` commits, `Plater::convert_unit`, `OrientJob` under a reporting wrapper | transform, size, optional job handle |
| `object_repair` | Close an object's open mesh | mutation | both | one object; one undo step | the repair command's per-part CGAL step, without its progress dialog | whether it changed; open edges, facets, parts and volume before and after; 32 `regionsUnbound` |
| `plan_set` | Pin the agent's plan and its reasoning | mutation (computation-only) | both | project-scoped product state | same | one headline, 16 decisions, 16 assumptions, 16 risks, 2 KB each |
| `plate_layout` | Set copies, what prints, which plate, names and filaments, add and name plates, and arrange | mutation | both | objects and plates in one undo step; arrange as a job | `Plater::increase_instances`/`decrease_instances`, the object list's printable toggle, `Selection` moves, `PartPlateList::create_plate`, `PartPlate::set_bed_type`, `ArrangeJob` | the objects section, added plate ids, optional job handle |
| `presets_list` | Choose a printer, filament, or process from what is installed | read-only | both | one preset kind | `PresetBundle` collections, read const | 25 per page with a cursor and the total |
| `printer_add` | Save the printer the person confirmed, so they can prepare prints for it | mutation, on the person's yes in the conversation | printer panel, every mode; refused outside an Add conversation | one catalog id and an optional nozzle it ships | `OrcaPrinterBackend::add_printer` (a named printer from the model's profile) | the printer as saved; `not_in_this_conversation`, `unknown_printer`, `unknown_nozzle`, `already_added`, `add_failed` |
| `printer_change` | Change a printer the person owns: the nozzle size now on it. What is loaded is the printer's to report, not a thing to save | mutation, on the person's yes in the conversation | printer panel, every mode | only the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; never the open project | `Printers::change_named_printer_nozzle` (writes the profile without selecting it) | what changed, before and after, and the printer as it now is; `no_printer`, `other_printer`, `unknown_printer`, `nothing_to_change`, `unknown_nozzle`, `change_failed` |
| `printer_connect` | Connect the printer the conversation is about | mutation; a card where the person types the access code or API key | printer panel, every mode | a Bambu Lab `deviceId` from the status, or a Moonraker or OctoPrint address the person gave | `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer`, `connect_host` | `connecting`, `verified` or `failed` with a message; the outcome of a wait arrives as a note; `no_printer`, `connection_unavailable`, `unknown_device`, `address_needed` |
| `printer_connection_status` | Know whether the printer can be reached, and which Bambu Lab printers are in LAN mode | read-only | printer panel, every mode | the printer the conversation is about | `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`, `prepare_connection` | provider, state, message, saved address and host type, LAN-mode candidates; `no_printer` |
| `printer_identify` | Show the printers the model decided the person means | read-only | printer panel, every mode; refused outside an Add conversation | 1 to 3 ids copied from the printer list in the instructions | `PrinterCatalog::panel_printers` | each printer's brand, model, build volume, nozzle sizes and what adding it assumes (nozzle; plate and filament, `null` where the profile names none); `not_in_this_conversation`, `too_many`, `unknown_printer`, `unknown_nozzle` |

content.text:
The refusal didn't fire because there was nothing to refuse: the conversation was an Add conversation from its first message. The model never switched from changing a printer to adding one. The app did that on purpose when the panel opened, because the printer your project selected is Bambu's stock profile, not one of your saved printers.

## Is the printer from the .3mf or your local settings?

It comes from the .3mf. The file's `Metadata/project_settings.config` names the printer profile `printer_settings_id = "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle"`, which is the stock Bambu Lab system profile. When the project opens, OrcaSlicer selects that stock profile. I checked the running app with `workspace_inspect`, and its selected printer preset is `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`.

That stock profile is not your saved printer. Your saved one is `Bambu Lab A1 mini 2.json` in `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/user/default/machine/`, which is built on top of the stock profile but is a separate preset. The header still says "Bambu Lab A1 mini" because, for a stock profile, the header shows the profile's model name ([SetupCommands.cpp:99](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:99)). So the header looks the same whether the selected printer is saved or stock.

## Why you got the "Which printer do you have?" conversation

1. "Printer settings…" in the header menu passes that label, "Bambu Lab A1 mini", as the printer name and asks for a Change conversation ([PrinterMenu.cpp:174](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:174)).
2. `PrinterConversation::start` finds no saved printer with that name and quietly switches the conversation to Add mode, on purpose ([PrinterConversation.cpp:164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:164)). Its comment says "A printer this app has not saved cannot be changed … Adding one is what there is to do." This dates from 8334b3395b (2026-09-23).
3. The refusals only apply to Change and Connect conversations, so in Add mode `printer_add` is allowed. It saved `Qidi X-Plus 4 (2).json` today at 16:20:44.

This is a design gap, not a failure of the refusal. You asked for the settings of the printer on screen, and the app sent you into adding a printer without saying why. I haven't changed any code for it. Possible directions:

- **Point to the saved printer:** say that the project uses Bambu's stock A1 mini profile, and offer to switch to your saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2".
- **Warn before adding:** keep the Add conversation, but open it with a note that the selected printer isn't one of your saved printers.
- **Open the settings instead:** for a stock profile, skip the conversation and open OrcaSlicer's own printer settings.

Tell me which one you want and I'll reproduce it in an isolated test copy of the app first.

## Docs and comment fixed

These changes are not committed.

- **[architecture.md:137](agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:137):** "eight printer tools" is now "five".
- **[mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md):**
  - "eight" is now "five" in two places.
  - `printer_manual_setup` is gone from the list of tools refused outside Add.
  - Added one sentence: the three tools were removed on 2026-09-28 in b60fc2d8e6, and the full printer list and printer settings are still reachable from the panel's own buttons.
  - Removed the tool-table rows for `printer_manual_connection`, `printer_manual_setup` and `printer_setup_finish`.
- **[App.tsx:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:403):** the comment now says Back is the only way the panel closes, because no tool closes it for the model. I checked that only the page's `close` action calls `close_panel`.

There's nothing to test here, since these are documentation and comment edits only.

are presets Uniquely identified by the name rather than an id in upstream orcaslcier?
Yes. Within one preset type, upstream OrcaSlicer identifies a preset by its name, and there is no separate local id.

* Name is the key. Preset.hpp:371 says: "The preset name shall be unique across a single PresetCollection." Each type (printers, filaments, processes) has its own `PresetCollection` (the list of all presets of that type), kept sorted by name. `find_preset(name)` at Preset.hpp:689 does a binary search on that name.
* Unique per type, not across types. A printer preset and a filament preset can share a name.
* What else resembles an id:
   * `setting_id` (Preset.hpp:288) is the preset's id in Bambu's cloud database, used only for cloud sync. Local lookups don't use it.
   * `alias` (Preset.hpp:266) is a display name shared by a family of stock filament presets. It is not unique.
   * `renamed_from` (Preset.hpp:270) lets a renamed stock profile still be found under its old name.
* Project files use names too. A .3mf records `printer_settings_id = "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle"`, and loading the project looks up that name.

This matters for the bug in one specific way. The fork's `PrinterConversation::saved()` (PrinterConversation.cpp:224) also matches by name. But "Printer settings…" passes it the header's label (PrinterMenu.cpp:174), not necessarily the preset name:

* For one of your saved printers, the label is the preset name, so the lookup works.
* For a stock profile, the label is `printer_model`, here "Bambu Lab A1 mini". The preset is actually named "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle".

Even with the full preset name, the lookup would still have missed, because the list it searches only contains your saved printers, never stock profiles. So the name mismatch didn't cause what you saw. It would matter if the menu is changed to pass the preset name so the conversation can recognize the stock profile and point you to your saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2".
</pasted_content id="f8db">

content.text:
Yes, I have four questions. The biggest is about scope: right now neither chat has a tool that can edit and save a printer or filament preset, so your second and third bullets mean building new tools, not just fixing name lookups.

## What the chats can do today

- **Printer chat** (the "Printer settings…" conversation on Home): its only editing tool, `printer_change`, saves a new nozzle size on one of your saved printers. It can't touch start G-code, bed size, or any other printer setting.
- **Filament chat** (the "Filament settings…" chat, which is the project assistant opened full-width): it can switch a slot to a different filament preset through `printer_setup`. It has no tool that edits a filament preset's settings.
- **Settings tools**: `settings_preview_patch` and `settings_apply_patch` only cover process settings. They also never save. They load the change into OrcaSlicer's process tab ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2354](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2354)), which leaves the preset showing as modified.

So no current tool fails with "this is a read-only system preset". Upstream OrcaSlicer lets you edit a system preset freely; only saving it is refused. Its save dialog then offers a new user preset named `<preset name> - Copy`. That is where your existing `Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle - Copy.json` came from.

## Generic errors

- **The fork:** a tool returns an error with a code and a message (`ToolError`, [ToolExecution.hpp:85](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecution.hpp:85)), and the model relays it to the person in the chat. For failures outside a tool call, the chat page shows a red error banner.
- **Upstream OrcaSlicer:** `show_error(parent, message)` ([GUI.cpp:249](src/slic3r/GUI/GUI.cpp:249)) opens a modal error dialog. Slicing and plater errors go to the notification area instead.

## Questions

1. **Scope.** Should I add tools that edit and save printer and filament preset settings, covering any setting in the preset (temperatures, start G-code, bed size and so on)? The printer chat would get the printer tool and the filament chat the filament tool. Or should this change only fix the name lookups, and let a found stock preset open its chat with today's tools?

2. **Saving and the copy.** When the person approves a change, should it be written to disk right away, like upstream's Save? And for a system preset, should the chat save it automatically as `<name> - Copy`, which is upstream's default, and then select that copy? For a printer, the copy becomes a new saved printer on Home. I'd recommend automatic, with the new name shown on the approval card, so there's no extra question.

3. **"Preset is changed later in the chat".** I read this as "later in the conversation the person asks for a change, and the chat calls the tool". Did you mean that, or the case where the person picks a different preset in the header while the chat is open?

4. **Preset not found.** The menu is built from the preset that's selected at that moment. So a lookup can only miss if the preset was renamed or deleted between building the menu and clicking the item, which shouldn't happen. The project rules say not to turn "impossible" states into quiet no-ops. So I'd recommend showing upstream's `show_error` dialog, not opening the chat, and letting the error reach Sentry. Is that OK, or do you want the chat to open and show the error?

Separately, whatever you answer, I'll change the three places in `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` that read `label(false)` to use `.name`, and make "Printer settings…" pass the preset name instead of the display label.

content.text:
You're right about the target. When the chat opens from Prepare, the named preset and the project's selected preset are the same one. They stay the same for the whole chat:
- The full-width chat hides the header, so the person can't pick a different preset while it's open.
- After a save-as-copy, the copy becomes the selected preset.

So I'll follow the documented contract: `scope=printer` is the selected printer preset and `scope=filament` is a project filament slot. The only place the two can differ is the Home printers column's own "Printer settings…", which can open a printer that isn't selected. That still goes to the Home printer conversation for nozzle and connection.

I couldn't find a commit that puts both the printer and filament chats full-width over Prepare, so I'm stopping here as you asked. The closest commits:

- **35be32c577** "Route printer and filament settings through focused chat" (jusprin-newui, 2026-09-28). Only filament goes full-width over Prepare (`ShellController::open_filament_help`). That chat is the project's saved assistant chat, not a separate in-memory one. The only printer change is that closing the Home printer panel returns to Prepare. The header's "Printer settings…" still switches to Home and opens the side panel.
- **2a07ec0fc7** "Give printer setup a focused workspace" (2026-09-22). This restyles the printer setup panel on Home. It doesn't put anything over Prepare.

I checked every local and remote branch, and none has a full-width printer chat. I also checked the other worktrees: the only matches for "focused" in shell or chat-page code are 35be32c577's.

Which commit did you mean? If it's on a branch or machine I can't see, give me its hash or branch name. Or, if 35be32c577 is the one, I'll use its full-width layout for both chats and back each with a separate in-memory chat instead of the project chat.

lines: - Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
-- Add-printer setup replaces Home with a centered conversation capped at 720 DIP (`component.printerSetup.contentWidth`), shrinking to fit the workspace. Existing-printer edits retain the sidebar.

+- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.

- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.
Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

content.content:
103:## Choose the narrowest honest scope
237:- unavailable operation: the requested scope has no active preset or target;
370:| `settings_apply_patch` | Apply the approved batch without overwriting a newer edit | mutation | both | currently process or object; required printer/filament expansion is specified below | `IWorkspace::apply_settings` through the owning config and `Tab::load_config` paths | bounded actual changes/normalization, revision, dirty flag and truthful `projectUndo` |
371:| `settings_get` | Read current values and preset origin | read-only | both | currently process or object; required printer/filament expansion is specified below | `IWorkspace::read_settings` using the scoped owner | at most 32 values and unknown-key issues; canonical values are preserved |
372:| `settings_preview_patch` | Check a batch before requesting approval | read-only | both | currently process or object; required printer/filament expansion is specified below | `IWorkspace::preview_settings` using a clone and scope-specific validation/normalization | at most 32 input keys; bounded changes, dependencies, issues and warnings |
373:| `settings_search` | Find a setting without loading the full catalog | read-only | both | currently process; required scope expansion is specified below | `IWorkspace::search_settings` using Orca definitions filtered by scope | 1–25 matches; deterministic cursor paging and bounded metadata |
402:`plate_layout` checks every row before anything moves, then applies plates (a row without an id adds one through the add-plate path, less its own snapshot), then objects: printable through the object list's own toggle steps, quantity through Orca's `increase_instances`/`decrease_instances` on the selected object (which refuse a disabled or cut object, and never with a count that would remove the object), a plate move as a relative move by the difference of plate origins, the name through the fork's `rename_object`, and the extruder as an object override. All of that is one "Lay out plates" undo step. Arrange sets the canvas spacing and rotation for the run and restores them when the job ends; with a plate id it arranges that plate (Orca's menu state), otherwise every unlocked plate. Orca does not report what did not fit (its `m_unarranged` is never filled), so the job's `notPlaced` is every printable instance no plate holds entirely afterwards. Two catalog details changed against the owner: `sequence` is not offered (print order is a per-plate setting and belongs with the settings tools), and arrange has no "selected" scope (`ArrangeJob` never calls its `prepare_selected`).
419:Four runs after the fixes. Runs 1 and 3 changed the process preset; run 3 skipped the brim, said so, and added it when asked (`brim_type` auto_brim → outer_only). Runs 2 and 4 put the same changes on the one object as overrides (`target`), which is a wrong-scope selection and an eval failure against the pinned model. That happened although the descriptions and the `target` property already said that a selected object or a single-object project is not a request for an override; wording alone has not fixed it. The project's setup card, which reads Orca's own preset deltas, showed exactly Brim type auto_brim → outer_only, Enable support 0 → 1, On build plate only 0 → 1 (the preset already had `tree(auto)`), and the harness check `verify_support_settings_patch` reads the native Support-page fields back after the same patch with a dialog counter installed. The live regression (`--live-agent`) at this point: 21 requests, 4,275 to 8,683 input tokens, 58 to 92 per cent cached.
447:**Fixes after the review (2026-09-17).** A plan is its source, its scope and its id together (`same_plan`): the in-app agent's scope is the chat (`planScope`, saved and sent to the page), an MCP plan has none. Before this, an MCP client and the in-app agent choosing the same id shared one plan, and Approve all on the external card also ran in-app members it did not list. A plan with a single member is drawn as an ordinary card once the in-app agent has finished proposing (and always, for MCP): `gpt-5.4-mini` sometimes gave a lone settings patch a `planId`, the page then showed a plan card, and the live regression's single-card decision never landed (3 runs in 4). The `planId` description now says to leave it out for one change. A slice starting, ending, or stopping being current publishes `WorkspaceChangeReasons::Slicing`, which is not in `kInvalidatingReasons`: it used to publish `Plates`, so the agent's own card-free `slice_start` failed every waiting card and a plan could not continue after its own slice. `Slicing` fails only a waiting `export_file` of a sliced kind, whose card names that slice's warnings. Still open: a plan cannot slice and then export, because `export_file` checks for a current slice when it is proposed, before the plan's slice has run.
466:`object_import` and `object_import_file` share `IWorkspace::import_objects`: `Plater::load_files` with `LoadModel` (plus `ImperialUnits` for inches) after selecting the target plate, under the same `ScopedModalAnswers` rule as `project_open`, returning the ids of every object the file added. The file tool looks only at the path before approval and shows it on the card. `project_delete_items` checks everything first, because some of Orca's refusals on these paths (the last solid part, the last copy) arrive as an error dialog after the call returns, which no scope can answer; it refuses deleting the solid parts of a cut object, answers the cut-object warning for a whole object with Delete (the card already named the object), drops parts and copies of objects deleted whole, deletes parts and copies through the object list in its expected order, then objects, then plates, whose objects Orca moves to another plate. Part ids come from the `partList` object_analyze now adds to `mesh`.
474:The implemented baseline covers the active FFF process preset and one object's overrides. The next settings milestone replaces that schema with the required four-scope contract in [Settings tools: contract and hazards](#settings-tools-contract-and-hazards); there is deliberately no compatibility mode for calls that omit `scope`. The process write allowlist is `writable_setting` in `SettingsSupport.hpp`: layers, walls, shells and infill (`layer_height`, `wall_loops`, `wall_generator`, `detect_thin_wall`, `only_one_wall_top`, the shell layer counts and thicknesses, infill density, direction and the three surface or infill patterns); the support family (`enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_style`, `support_threshold_angle`, `support_on_build_plate_only`, the interface layer counts and pattern, and the top and bottom contact distances); adhesion and seam (`brim_type`, `brim_width`, `skirt_loops`, `skirt_distance`, `seam_position`); and ten speed keys. `settings_search` takes `writable` to list only the requested scope's allowlist and `changedOnly` to list only keys that differ from that scope's saved preset or inherited value. Apply takes `scope`, the scope's exact target when required, `changes`, `expectedSessionId`, and `expectedRevision` from a fresh preview. Native approval captures the exact before/after values, including normalization dependencies, then revalidates before applying. It publishes one `Settings` revision, updates native fields and dirty state, and invalidates slicing. Use the owning preset's revert control or a previewed inverse patch to restore preset values; ordinary project Undo reverses object overrides but not process, filament, or printer preset edits.
509:| `settings_search` | R | Required `scope`; required `target` for `object` and `filament`, forbidden otherwise; `writable` and `changedOnly` filters. `changedOnly` answers what differs from the owning preset or inherited value. | `print_config_def`; scoped edited preset or `ModelConfig`; dirty options | 25 per page |
510:| `settings_get` | R | Required `scope` and its exact target; origin reported as system, user preset, project edit, filament preset, printer preset, or object override. | scoped edited presets; `PresetBundle::filament_presets`; `ModelConfig` | 32 keys |
511:| `settings_preview_patch` | R | Required `scope` and its exact target; applies the scope-specific writable allowlist, dependencies, validation, persistence and undo semantics. | scope-specific config clone; `ConfigManipulation` where applicable; `Slic3r::validate` | 32 keys |
512:| `settings_apply_patch` | M | Required `scope` and the same target as preview. Optional `persistAs` is valid only for preset scopes, saves the result as a named user preset in the same approval, and makes the call destructive. | owning `Tab` and `PresetCollection`; `ModelConfig` for object | 32 keys |
592:| `calibration_generate` | M | Generate one test's geometry and configuration onto a new plate. Analysis is reasoning over a photo or camera frame; applying a result uses `settings_apply_patch` on the filament scope with `persistAs`. | `CalibUtils` generators | |
596:Reads folded into `workspace_inspect` sections: project details, intent, printer state and mismatches, confirmed facts, monitoring policy, object manifest, plan, activity state, history, versions. ## Settings tools: contract and hazards

The settings tools are the reference implementation of this guide. What
follows is the part of their design that stays true after the work is done;
the implementation handoff that produced it is retired. Re-read this section
before expanding the write allowlist or adding a tool that changes a preset.

### Standing decisions

1. Settings are data: four generic tools over searchable records, never one
   tool per setting.
2. Every settings call requires `scope`, whose enum is exactly `process`,
   `object`, `filament`, or `printer`. Missing scope is `invalid_arguments`.
   There is no default, inference from `target`, alias, or compatibility mode.
3. `target` is scope-dependent and closed:

   | `scope` | `target` | Meaning |
   |---|---|---|
   | `process` | forbidden | the active edited FFF process preset |
   | `object` | required `{objectId}` | that object's `ModelConfig` overrides |
   | `filament` | required `{filamentIndex}` | the preset used by that 1-based project filament index |
   | `printer` | forbidden | the active edited FFF printer preset |

   These rules apply to `settings_search`, `settings_get`,
   `settings_preview_patch`, and `settings_apply_patch`. Reject an extra,
   missing, zero-based, or wrong-shaped target as `invalid_arguments`.
4. Scope identifies the settings owner; it does not select a preset.
   `printer_setup` remains the only tool that switches printer, process, or
   filament presets. Settings tools edit the already selected owner and must
   never switch a preset, discard dirty edits, change nozzle topology, or
   substitute a compatible profile as a side effect.
5. Metadata, parsing, and serialization come from Orca's own
   `print_config_def` and config option machinery. There is no parallel table
   of types, enum values, ranges, units, or aliases.
6. Search and read cover every definition applicable to the requested scope;
   mutation has a separate reviewed allowlist per scope. Every search and read
   record says whether the key is writable; other keys return
   `unsupported_setting_mutation`. Expand an allowlist only after real-adapter
   tests cover the option type, dependency behavior, visible UI update, dirty
   state, persistence and undo/revert behavior for that scope.
7. A batch applies whole or not at all, through `Tab::load_config` or the
   scope's existing owner path. Never mutate a config behind the visible
   preset UI and imitate the notifications.
8. Process, filament, and printer preset edits are not in project Undo.
   Results say `projectUndo: false` and return previous values so a caller can
   propose an inverse. Object overrides use one Orca snapshot and return
   `projectUndo: true`.
9. Every result echoes the validated `scope`, normalized `target`, owning
   `presetName` when there is one, `sessionId`, and `revision`. Filament
   results also return `affectedFilamentIndices`, because several project
   filament indices may use the same preset.
10. A preview that finds invalid settings is a successful call with
   `valid: false`. Malformed input is a tool error.
11. All values cross JSON as strings in their canonical Orca serialization;
   callers may send numbers or booleans and the decoder converts them. All
   Orca ids cross JSON as strings.

The schema change is intentionally breaking. This interface does not need a
backward-compatibility period: update the in-app adapter, MCP projection,
deterministic agent, fixtures, and eval prompts in the same change. Do not add
a protocol-version branch, feature flag, alias, fallback, or migration path
for the old missing-scope or implicit-object forms. After the change, every
caller must send the new contract.

### Scope-specific ownership

- **Process:** the active `prints.get_edited_preset()` and
  `Tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)`. The implemented normalizer, validation, dirty
  state, approval binding, and inverse-patch rules below continue to apply.
- **Object:** the selected `ModelObject`'s `ModelConfig`, identified only by
  `target.objectId`. The implemented project-Undo behavior below continues to
  apply.
- **Filament:** `target.filamentIndex` is 1-based and resolves through
  `PresetBundle::filament_presets` to a named filament preset. Search, get and
  preview resolve it without changing the selected filament tab. Preview and
  apply bind that index, resolved preset name, every before value, and the set
  of other project filament indices that use the same preset. A changed
  mapping or preset is `stale_workspace`. Apply must use the filament preset
  owner and `Tab(Preset::TYPE_FILAMENT)` without silently switching away from
  or discarding another dirty edited preset; if Orca cannot do that safely,
  return `unsaved_edits`. The result names every affected index.
- **Printer:** the active `printers.get_edited_preset()` and
  `Tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINTER)`. Generic settings mutation does not select a
  printer or change hardware identity. The initial writable allowlist excludes
  topology and compatibility keys such as extruder count, nozzle layout, and
  printer technology until their substitutions are modeled and tested; those
  setup changes stay in `printer_setup`.

`persistAs` is invalid for `object`. For `process`, `filament`, or `printer`,
it saves the post-patch config as a named user preset only after preview and
approval show the destination and overwrite behavior. Without `persistAs`,
the tool changes only the edited preset and leaves it dirty.

### Scope expansion acceptance criteria

- The registry exposes the same required `scope` enum and target shape through
  the in-app and MCP adapters; catalog tests pin both projections.
- Argument tests reject omitted or unknown scopes and every missing, extra,
  zero-based, mixed, or malformed target. No test accepts the old call shape.
- Search, get, preview, and apply each have fake- and real-adapter coverage for
  all four scopes, including a readable but unwritable key.
- Filament tests cover index-to-preset resolution, two indices sharing one
  preset, a mapping that becomes stale, and a dirty preset that cannot be
  changed without an implicit switch or discard.
- Printer tests prove that a normal writable value updates the native field,
  dirty marker, slice invalidation, and read-back value, while topology and
  compatibility keys remain unwritable.
- Apply tests prove atomic failure, scope-specific approval text, preset revert
  or inverse-patch behavior, and project Undo only for object overrides.
- Evals and deterministic-agent fixtures use explicit scopes before the old
  schema is removed; there is no dual-schema phase.

### Error codes

| Condition | Code |
|---|---|
| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target` | `invalid_arguments` |
| key not in the definition table | `unknown_setting` with suggestions |
| known key not applicable to the requested scope | `unsupported_scope` |
| readable key outside that scope's allowlist | `unsupported_setting_mutation` |
| requested object, filament index, or owning preset is gone | `workspace_unavailable` |
| applying a filament target would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |
| parse failure, bound violation, or layer height outside the printer's range | `invalid_setting_value` with `allowed` or bounds |
| a scope-specific dependency or validator rule conflicts | `incompatible_settings` with the conflicting keys |
| session, revision, target mapping, preset, or before value changed since preview | `stale_workspace` with expected and current |
| user rejected in JusPrin | `approval_rejected` |
| client cancelled or the app closed | `cancelled` |
| the batch call failed after validation | `execution_failed` |

Preview never fails for content reasons. Apply fails with the first blocking
code and mutates nothing. Never convert an invariant failure into success.

### Orca entry points the tools use

- **Process atomic batch:** `Tab::load_config(const DynamicPrintConfig&)` in
  `src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp` diffs against the edited preset, sets every changed
  key, then runs `update_dirty()`, `reload_config()`, and `update()` once.
  `TabPrint::update()` runs the FFF normalizer and reaches
  `Plater::on_config_change`, which invalidates slicing as a sidebar edit
  would. Apply is therefore: build a config holding only the changed keys and
  call `wxGetApp().get_tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)->load_config(diff)`.

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='mcp-tool-extension-guide.md'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(o,n):
    global s
    assert s.count(o)==1,(s.count(o),o[:80]); s=s.replace(o,n)

rep('''   | `filament` | required `{filamentIndex}` | the preset used by that 1-based project filament index |
   | `printer` | forbidden | the active edited FFF printer preset |

   These rules apply to `settings_search`, `settings_get`,
   `settings_preview_patch`, and `settings_apply_patch`. Reject an extra,
   missing, zero-based, or wrong-shaped target as `invalid_arguments`.
4. Scope identifies the settings owner; it does not select a preset.
   `printer_setup` remains the only tool that switches printer, process, or
   filament presets. Settings tools edit the already selected owner and must
   never switch a preset, discard dirty edits, change nozzle topology, or
   substitute a compatible profile as a side effect.''','''   | `filament` | required `{preset}` | that filament preset, by name |
   | `printer` | required `{preset}` | that printer preset, by name |

   These rules apply to `settings_search`, `settings_get`,
   `settings_preview_patch`, and `settings_apply_patch`. Reject an extra,
   missing, empty, or wrong-shaped target as `invalid_arguments`.
   A preset is named the way Orca keys it: by its name, unique within its
   own collection (`Preset.hpp`: "The preset name shall be unique across a
   single PresetCollection"). Never by the label a menu shows -- the header
   shows a stock printer's model, and `Preset::label` puts `"* "` in front of
   a preset with unsaved edits -- and never by an alias. A name no visible
   preset has is `unknown_preset`, whose suggestions are the project's
   filaments or the printer in use. (The first draft of this contract named a
   filament by its 1-based project slot and edited only the selected printer;
   on 2026-09-29 Kenneth chose the preset's name for both, so a chat opened
   for one preset, and a saved printer the project does not use, can be
   changed without selecting anything first.)
4. Scope identifies the settings owner; `printer_setup` remains the only tool
   that picks the project's printer, process, or filament. A settings call
   never discards dirty edits, changes nozzle topology, or substitutes a
   compatible profile. It selects a preset only where Orca's own Save or edit
   path does: a copy saved with `persistAs` takes the original's place, and a
   filament that is not the one open in its tab is opened there the way the
   sidebar's edit button opens it (`PlaterPresetComboBox::switch_to_tab`).''')

rep('''9. Every result echoes the validated `scope`, normalized `target`, owning
   `presetName` when there is one, `sessionId`, and `revision`. Filament
   results also return `affectedFilamentIndices`, because several project
   filament indices may use the same preset.''','''9. Every result echoes the validated `scope`, the owning `presetName` (the
   process preset for an object), `sessionId`, and `revision`. An apply also
   returns `savedAs`, the name it saved under or empty, and `presetDirty`.''')

rep('''- **Filament:** `target.filamentIndex` is 1-based and resolves through
  `PresetBundle::filament_presets` to a named filament preset. Search, get and
  preview resolve it without changing the selected filament tab. Preview and
  apply bind that index, resolved preset name, every before value, and the set
  of other project filament indices that use the same preset. A changed
  mapping or preset is `stale_workspace`. Apply must use the filament preset
  owner and `Tab(Preset::TYPE_FILAMENT)` without silently switching away from
  or discarding another dirty edited preset; if Orca cannot do that safely,
  return `unsaved_edits`. The result names every affected index.
- **Printer:** the active `printers.get_edited_preset()` and
  `Tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINTER)`. Generic settings mutation does not select a
  printer or change hardware identity. The initial writable allowlist excludes
  topology and compatibility keys such as extruder count, nozzle layout, and
  printer technology until their substitutions are modeled and tested; those
  setup changes stay in `printer_setup`.

`persistAs` is invalid for `object`. For `process`, `filament`, or `printer`,
it saves the post-patch config as a named user preset only after preview and
approval show the destination and overwrite behavior. Without `persistAs`,
the tool changes only the edited preset and leaves it dirty.''','''- **Filament and printer, the preset being edited** (the one selected in its
  collection): its edited copy and its `Tab`, as for the process. Reads
  include its unsaved edits.
- **Filament, another preset:** must be in one of the project's slots
  (`not_in_project`), and changes only by being saved (`not_selected` without
  `persistAs`). Apply opens it in the filament tab as the sidebar's edit
  button does -- `Tab::select_preset`, then `set_filament_idx` for its slot --
  then loads and saves through the tab. If the filament open in the tab has
  unsaved edits, that switch would discard or prompt, so preview refuses with
  `unsaved_edits`.
- **Printer, another preset:** a saved printer the project does not use,
  saved in place only (`Printers::write_unselected_printer`, the write
  `change_named_printer_nozzle` already makes: the difference from its parent,
  queued for the cloud). A copy of it would be a second printer made behind
  the project's back, so a different `persistAs` is `not_selected`.
- The printer allowlist (`writable_printer_setting`) is custom g-code,
  printable height, layer-height limits, Z offset, retraction and machine
  limits. It excludes the keys that decide which filament and process fit, or
  how many extruders there are -- bed shape, nozzle size and type, extruder
  count, printer model -- which change with `printer_setup` or
  `printer_change`. The filament allowlist (`writable_filament_setting`) is
  temperatures, cooling, flow, pressure advance, volumetric speed, density,
  cost and custom g-code.
- A setting that holds one value per extruder or per nozzle kind keeps its
  length: a patch with a different number of values is
  `invalid_setting_value`, since a shorter list would drop the rest.

`persistAs` is invalid for `object`. It is Orca's Save with the name typed
in: the preset's own name overwrites it (`read_only_preset` for one Orca
ships, with `"<name> - Copy"`, the name SavePresetDialog offers, as the
suggestion); another name that no preset has saves a copy that takes the
original's place, in every project slot that used it for a filament
(`Sidebar::update_presets_from_to`); a name another preset has is
`name_taken`; a name SavePresetDialog would refuse is `invalid_preset_name`.
Saving the preset being edited also saves its other unsaved edits, as Save
does; preview warns with `saves_unsaved_edits` and lists them. The card's
title says where it saves ("; save it", or "; save as \\"<name>\\""). Without
`persistAs`, the tool changes only the edited preset and leaves it dirty.

Dialogs the filament and printer tabs would open are refused in preview:
a max volumetric speed below 0.5 (`ConfigManipulation::
check_filament_max_volumetric_speed`), a first-layer temperature further
from the other layers' than `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs`
allows when saving, and firmware retraction with a wipe that retracts less
than 100% first (`TabPrinter::toggle_options`).''')

rep('''- Filament tests cover index-to-preset resolution, two indices sharing one
  preset, a mapping that becomes stale, and a dirty preset that cannot be
  changed without an implicit switch or discard.''','''- Filament tests cover a preset in a slot that is not open in its tab, a copy
  taking its slot, and a dirty preset that cannot be changed without an
  implicit switch or discard.''')

rep('''| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target` | `invalid_arguments` |''','''| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target`; `persistAs` for an object | `invalid_arguments` |
| no visible preset of that scope has the target's name | `unknown_preset` with suggestions |
| a filament or printer preset that is not being edited, without `persistAs`, or a copy of a printer not in use | `not_selected` |
| a filament that is in none of the project's slots, changed by name | `not_in_project` |
| `persistAs` overwriting a preset Orca ships | `read_only_preset`, suggesting `"<name> - Copy"` |
| `persistAs` naming another existing preset | `name_taken` |
| `persistAs` SavePresetDialog would refuse | `invalid_preset_name` |''')
rep('''| requested object, filament index, or owning preset is gone | `workspace_unavailable` |
| applying a filament target would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |''','''| requested object is gone, or no FFF printer or process is selected | `workspace_unavailable` |
| opening a filament in its tab would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
echo done

**Status:** Extension guide for the implemented shared registry, embedded MCP server, and stdio bridge. The MCP catalog includes workspace inspection, slice-review reporting, and the verified process/object-settings workflow. A [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog) derived from the product surface

New capabilities are added to the shared registry, executed by `ToolExecutionCoordinator`, and implemented through the typed live-workspace boundary; the OpenAI and MCP adapters only translate that contract to their wire formats. This guide keeps t
- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the five printer tools and no others, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. lines: -**Status:** Extension guide for the implemented shared registry, embedded MCP server, and stdio bridge. The MCP catalog includes workspace inspection, slice-review reporting, and the verified process/object-settings workflow. A [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog) derived from the product surfaces follows the implemented catalog record; nothing in it exists unless the catalog record says so.

+**Status:** Extension guide for the implemented shared registry, embedded MCP server, and stdio bridge. The MCP catalog includes workspace inspection, slice-review reporting, and the settings workflow over the process, one object, and filament and printer presets. A [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog) derived from the product surfaces follows the implemented catalog record; nothing in it exists unless the catalog record says so.

JusPrin has one tool system with multiple adapters. New capabilities are added to the shared registry, executed by `ToolExecutionCoordinator`, and implemented through the typed live-workspace boundary; the OpenAI and MCP adapters only translate that contract to their wire formats. This guide keeps the catalog small, honest, safe to evolve, and driven by real printing tasks rather than an abstract feature inventory.

The `--live-agent` regression at both points says what that costs. The first request of a conversation caches nothing and pays for the whole catalog: 803 tokens at M0, 1,733 at M1, so four more definitions cost about 930 tokens, once. Every later request in the same conversation came back 77 to 92 per cent cached (5,864 in, 5,376 cached at M1), because the tools array is byte-identical across a chat and that is what the cache keys on. At M2 the same regression's eleven requests took 2,875 to 6,763 input tokens with 42 to 91 per cent cached; none started cold, because an earlier run of the same day had warmed the cache for the shared prefix, so the M2 cold cost is not measured by that run.

So the cost of a definition is what it adds to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn, and the budget stays a trigger rather than a gate. What would change that reading: a catalog large enough to make the first request of every conversation expensive on its own, or transcripts showing the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch both; neither has appeared yet.

-- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the five printer tools and no others, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer. A list that differs by mode is not used: the conversation's own refusal is needed whatever the model is shown, and a restricted-but-stable list (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. What would change that: transcripts of the model reaching for a refused tool and not recovering, which `tests/printer_prompt` measures (`change-add-another`). Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). On 2026-09-28 the three tools that opened a window or closed the panel -- `printer_manual_setup`, `printer_manual_connection` and `printer_setup_finish` -- were removed (b60fc2d8e6): OrcaSlicer's full printer list and a printer's settings stay reachable from the panel's own buttons, and the person closes the panel. The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.

What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer; the settings tools only with `scope: "printer"` on the printer the conversation is about. Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.

- **Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Use the platform's own deferral, never a hand-rolled switcher. On the in-app side that is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API, documented for `gpt-5.4` and later; support on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unverified. On the MCP side clients defer on their own, as Claude Code does. Toolsets are the deferral unit, and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. An enable-toolset tool that rewrites the tools array breaks the prompt cache on every switch and is not to be built.

- **Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing a slicer user would name: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Not a wrapper per Orca function, and not an interpreter for a list of unrelated commands. Optional facets of one operation are fine when each is independently typed and conflicting facets are rejected.

- **Batch only where items share a shape.** A list of setting changes, a list of intent fields, a list of annotations, a list of per-object layout rows. A list that mixes transforms, imports, and deletes is the god tool and is refused.
- `workspace_inspect` is exposed to both adapters so either can obtain a fresh completed slice identity after slicing, independently of the initial turn context;

- attachment-based import (`object_import`) is in-app-only, and path-based `object_import_file` is MCP-only, because a file reaches the app through the conversation in one case and through an approved path in the other; that is two honest definitions over one workspace command, not one tool with forked behavior; and
- a future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP-only if it exists to establish the external connection; and

-- the printer panel's five tools carry only the `Printer` exposure: neither adapter lists them, and the panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses what does not fit it (see "Tool budget and tool shape"). They take no `planId` (`joins_plans` excludes them), and what the model reads back from them is the tool's own result, not the host's workspace envelope.

Document the reason beside the registry definition and test it. Exposure is not a place to fork behavior: if two adapters need different semantics, they need a better shared command or honestly separate definitions.

| `record_physical_print` | Record a completed print fact | destructive | Internal | manufacturing history; does not start a printer | coordinator's history recorder | physical-print ID, build ID and recorded flag |

The three fixtures are retired, each in the change that landed its replacement: `duplicate_object` with `plate_layout` (the tests that used it as their canonical mutation now propose one more copy through `plate_layout` and count instances, and so do the deterministic mock agent and the live regression), `import_model` with `object_import` (the import tests, the mock agent's attachment reply and the bridge test now use it), and `inspect_selection` with the summary's selection ids (the canonical read-only action in the tests is now `workspace_inspect`). `tests/agent/test_tool_registry.cpp` pins the exact exposed-name lists, so every retirement is visible in that test's diff.

The process write allowlist is `writable_setting` in `SettingsSupport.hpp`: layers, walls, shells and infill (`layer_height`, `wall_loops`, `wall_generator`, `detect_thin_wall`, `only_one_wall_top`, the shell layer counts and thicknesses, infill density, direction and the three surface or infill patterns); the support family (`enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_style`, `support_threshold_angle`, `support_on_build_plate_only`, the interface layer counts and pattern, and the top and bottom contact distances); adhesion and seam (`brim_type`, `brim_width`, `skirt_loops`, `skirt_distance`, `seam_position`); and ten speed keys. `settings_search` takes `writable` to list only the requested scope's allowlist and `changedOnly` to list only keys that differ from that scope's saved preset or inherited value. lines: The printer panel is the example. The app sends the page facts only: sizes, spools, which printer is on a card, what a change changed. The page writes every word from them. It writes the model's instructions (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`) and hands them over with `printer_instructions`. It writes the panel's own words, the opening line and the note that goes with each tap (`AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`). The opening goes over with `printer_opening`, and a tap's note travels in the tap's payload.

-The app decides the tools -- the five printer tools, the same in every mode -- checks every call, refuses one that does not fit the conversation (adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one it is about), and refuses a turn that has no instructions rather than falling back to the project assistant's prompt. It posts the opening once per session, and a tap's note only when the tap goes through, bounded to 2 KB. It still writes the notes for what only it can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, its model id is not on the list, or a save or undo failed.

+The app decides the tools -- the five printer tools and the four settings tools, the same in every mode -- checks every call, refuses one that does not fit the conversation (adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one it is about, a setting of anything but that printer), and refuses a turn that has no instructions rather than falling back to the project assistant's prompt. It posts the opening once per session, and a tap's note only when the tap goes through, bounded to 2 KB. It still writes the notes for what only it can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, its model id is not on the list, or a save or undo failed.

Windows uses WebView2, macOS uses WKWebView, and Linux uses WebKitGTK. Local resource packaging must work on all three. The demonstrated prototype used a single-file local bundle to avoid WKWebView `file:` subresource failures; production keeps that approach, and CMake now produces the bundle from the TypeScript/React sources.
